technology.summary: Today's technology news includes Microsoft's announcement of its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. Amazon's use of over 1 million robot workers raises questions about the future of human employees. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will explore how to build enduring companies in the AI era. Other stories include the launch of the Fitbit Edge, the rise of AI apps that listen to users, and Apple's upcoming "Welcome Home" event, where new smart home products are expected to be unveiled.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have joined forces to simplify regulatory procedures for foreign portfolio investors. This comes as the Nifty index is under pressure, with foreign portfolio investors recording a net sale of shares worth Rs 10,148 crore. Indian equity benchmarks have also experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court of India has urged a probe into reports of hospitals enforcing steep markups on cancer drugs, leading to a 5% drop in the BSE Hospitals Index.

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai, while Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC for executing illegal orders. In other news, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt', citing an Indian election that didn't happen, and Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
